title: What's Cooking in Business Central: Replace Permission Sets Upon Import

chapters.title: Introduction and permission sets use case
Import behavior in previous versions - merge approach
Alternative use case - replacing instead of merging

features.name: Replace permission sets upon import
features.description: New capability in 2025 wave 2 release that allows users to replace existing permission sets with imported ones instead of merging them. When selecting no during import prompt, the system replaces existing permissions entirely.
features.status_evidence_quote: what's coming in the 2025 wave 2 release
caveats: Requires selecting no when prompted to update existing permissions

features.name: Import permission sets action
features.description: Existing action that imports permission sets from files. Previous versions merged permissions from test and production environments when confirming yes. Now provides option to replace instead of merge.

quotes.text: If you frequently work with permission sets, you'll be interested to hear what's coming in the 2025 wave 2 release.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes that this feature is a forthcoming capability in 2025 wave 2, not yet available.

quotes.text: When using the action import permission sets in previous version of Business Central, the system would ask whether we want to update it.
quotes.why_it_matters: Documents the existing behavior and the upgrade path for this feature.

quotes.text: If we confirmed with yes, the system would behave as expected, merging permissions from the test and production environment.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the previous default behavior of merging rather than replacing permissions.

quotes.text: To overrite the existing permissions instead of merging them we must select no when prompted.
quotes.why_it_matters: Describes the new mechanism: selecting no enables replace instead of merge behavior.

quotes.text: After choosing no, we see that the permissions were not merged. Instead, the vendor table was removed and contacts were added exactly as defined
quotes.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the replace functionality working as designed, with exact matching of imported permissions.

quotes.text: With this improvement, you no longer have to manually delete existing permissions before importing a new set.
quotes.why_it_matters: States the practical benefit of the replace option over the previous merge-only behavior.

disclaimers.text: what's coming in the 2025 wave 2 release
